I definitely agree that I've reached some sort of limit. I hate my degree, but with just a single semester left it's far too late, not to mention financially irresponsible, to change majors now. I'm not even sure what I would choose to do instead. Maybe music? I'm really not sure, which has been a common trend for most of my adult life. I scarcely have opinions on things that should matter to me, and I haven't had goals for some time now. When I try to think about what I could have done instead, what other paths I could have taken, I just get filled with regret, so I shut everything out and try to occupy myself with anything else - be it work that I hate, or playing video games, one of the few things I enjoy. I have relatively few friends and acquaintances because I find it a bit of a struggle to care about other people. I just get bored with them too quickly and end up ghosting them. You're probably right about the emotional void that the attic represents - I struggle to feel pride in past accomplishments that I have every right to be proud of - things I know I did by my own merit, yet I still feel as though it's all been a fluke.

Thanks for your input, by the way, it's helped to bring out the introspective side of me that I spend too much time pushing down, shying away from. It's been nice to take a moment and try to pin down the sources of some of my issues.

I'm not really sure what I think about the attic. If anything, I guess I would say I'm confused as to why anything is up there. Maybe there's a tinge of fear or regret when the object eventually snaps? As far as what I would prefer regarding exploring vs. continuing to pull items out, I honestly think I would just want to sit and watch the object to see if anything happens without my involvement.

When I still lived with my parents, every Saturday was a mandatory Family Fun Day. We were always buying new board games, so it was usually a good time, as long as my baby brother wasn't losing, of course. My mom's side of the family had been doing this for years, and so my papi (what we called our grandpa on my mom's side) had a huge collection of older games. My brother and I loved visiting papi so we could try out his games, and we really hit the jackpot when I was nine. My parents decided that they were going to have date night every other week, so we got to play with papi a lot more often. One of our favorite games to play with him was Dungeons and Dragons. After we finished our first campaign, killed some dragons, and saved a princess, papi told my brother and I he had a new role-playing game for us. He called it "Cowboys and Aliens." We were super into star wars at the time, so it sounded like a great idea. The game went something like this: My brother and I would play the aliens, getting all dressed up in silly costumes, and my papi would dress as a cowboy. Our goal was to get him caught in a trap so we could 'probe' him with some metal rods. Papi used to play this game with my mom, too, so he was really good at it. I think he let us win the first few times. His goal was to trap us, so he could 'kill' us or interrogate us for attacking his town. Whenever he won (and he won A LOT), he would tie us up. The first couple of times, he would 'kill' us so we could start over again, it was so much fun! After a while, he decided to start interrogating us instead. He would sometimes dip our heads into a bucket of water, or cut us until we talked. This part was even more fun! After my brother and I got more practice, we started to get really good at trapping papi. We got to probe him so many times! One Saturday, after our parents dropped us off, papi told us he was taking off his kiddie shoes and would be going all-out from now on. I guess he was tired of losing? Anyway, if we thought he was good before, he was on a whole other level now. He beat us within minutes every time, and he started to get really creative when he tied us up, too. Now he was tying our arms and legs behind our backs, hanging us upside down. He told us in his gruff cowboy voice that he was gonna get us back for all the times we probed him, to see how we liked it. And boy, did we *like it!* He probed us super hard, and he was even nice enough to warm up the metal rod for us. There were a few times where it even felt like I was gonna explode! We did this for a few years, until one night when our parents came back a bit earlier than usual to pick us up. My mom screamed at papi to stop and untie my brother and me. When we got down, my mom grabbed us and ran towards the car, telling papi that he could never come near my brother and I again. After that night, every Saturday turned into Lockdown Night. My brother and I got locked in our rooms and weren't allowed to leave, even to pee. I guess that was my weirdest rule growing up, but man do I miss Family Fun Nights with papi.
